text:
maya: heads-up — onboarding customer BrightForms is hitting intermittent 502/504s on hosted inference when they use streaming with chunked transfer and additional metadata trailers. happens ~10-25s into the stream, looks like upstream reset. sample curl repro below. tagging @dan and @eli :eyes:

maya: repro curl (sanitized) — they say this reliably fails for payloads > ~128KB:
```
curl -v \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \n  --data-binary @large_prompt.json \n  'https://api.hosted.redwood.com/v1/generate?model=gpt-x-stream'
```

maya: server-side snippet from their trace (trimmed):
```
[envoy upstream reset] stream_id=0x7f2 client_conn=0x3a: remote close, code=RESET, reason="upstream_connection_reset"
[proxy] 502 response to client, request_id=bf4c-1729, upstream_latency=11530ms
```

dan: thanks — do we have our trace/req id from the edge for their failed requests? need to correlate with ingress logs and tenant_id. any pattern on region/model?

maya: trace id they provided: br-1729-bf4c. hitting in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, both with same symptoms. model is streaming small-token outputs but large initial input.

eli: quick thoughts: chunked + trailers can trigger buffering differences in nginx/Envoy. if proxy buffering is disabled on NGINX or blob larger than proxy_buffer_size in Envoy, upstream may close while downstream still streaming. also watch proxy_read_timeout and keepalive windows. can you grab full edge logs for request_id bf4c-1729?

support-oncall: escalation opened: INC-2024-3857, assigned to eng-infra. collecting tcpdump + edge nginx logs. pushed repro steps to the ticket. :white_check_mark:

maya: reproduced locally in staging by feeding a 200KB prompt with chunked transfer — I see a RESET from upstream at ~12s. attaching staging curl run and the edge tail: 
```
<staging> envoy: "upstream reset: connection terminated by peer" request_id=bf4c-1729
<staging> nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection" while reading response header from upstream
```

eli: can you try toggling proxy_buffering and proxy_request_buffering? on nginx, setting proxy_request_buffering off for the route avoids nginx consuming body into temp files and seems to reduce upstream resets for streaming large chunked bodies. also increase proxy_read_timeout and proxy_buffers as a mitigation. config snippet: 
```nginx
location /v1/generate/ {
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 120s;
  proxy_buffers 8 32k;
}
```

dan: for Envoy fronting we should also check upstream_conn_pool settings and cluster max_connections. increasing maxConnectionDuration and timeouts can help. I'll query edge metrics for stream resets and connection dropped counts over the last hour.

maya: tried nginx toggles in staging — proxy_request_buffering off reduced frequency (still see a couple), proxy_buffering off made it near-deterministic pass for the curl repro.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: snapshot config change staged to edge-nodes (nginx): set proxy_request_buffering=off for /v1/generate in canary group (3/30 nodes). watch for errors and latency regressions.

support-oncall: asking BrightForms to retry against canary host and provide new trace ids. also requesting they try with and without trailers (some clients append metadata as trailers).

eli: long-term: we should add a routing rule for streaming endpoints that enforces request buffering off and higher timeouts, and add automated test with chunked+trailer payloads to catch regressions. filing infra task.

dan: noted. I'm collecting metrics now, will post a quick chart. if canary looks good after 30m we can roll. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
